decisions.evidence: Accepted the reader's corrected commutator and toral multiplication. Read Definition and Verification 1.1–7.1 and exact dependency interfaces (DJ presentation, half grading, quantum integers, triangular decomposition, Chevalley involutions, root height). Word recursion produces coefficients in the actual quotient; independence of 1 and K_i^2 follows from nonzero independent h_i and the toral basis, so uniqueness supplies descent and linearity. Prefix crossings have opposite signs for e_i' and e_i'', actual wt(F_j)=-alpha_j; empty word, zero, one-letter and vanishing degree are covered. Bar swaps the coefficients and reverses the denominator. JKK §6 (6.1)–(6.3), printed p.22, agrees with this convention. No AC is needed for triangular decomposition (i)–(ii).

Accepted clearing negative Laurent powers and the corrected common-denominator tensor identity. Read Definition, Facts and Verification 1.1–7.1 with Laurent-ring, datum, quantum integer and DJ/half interfaces; rank-one string supplier is convention-only. Every toral denominator is nonzero at generic q, and the homogeneous generators give a direct root grading. Fraction-field tensor injectivity uses U_A as a submodule of the ambient field-vector space, not freeness over Z[q,q^-1]. The ideal (2,q-1) is proper by augmentation; the mod-2 domain argument proves nonprincipality. Empty products and r=t=0 give 1. No global integral PBW assertion is imported and no choice is used.

Accepted the corrected integrability counterexamples and declared rank-one supplier. Read the chosen label grading, Definition/Facts/Verification 1.1–4.1, quantum datum/DJ interfaces, classical weight convention and rank-one strings. Toral characters agree exactly when the integer pairings agree, with a direct-sum eigenspace consisting of all matching labels; separating pairings recover the usual eigenspaces. The explicit P=Z^2, alpha=(2,0) witness satisfies the datum and merges labels only spectrally. Kernels and quotients require graded maps/submodules. Local nilpotence survives submodules/quotients and finite-support direct sums; countably many trivial copies give infinite weight dimension, and the rank-one strings give unbounded support. The zero module satisfies both nilpotence conditions with exponent 1. No finite weight-dimension or finite-cone assumption is smuggled into integrability; no choice is used.

Accepted the corrected Serre scalar and the uniqueness argument that does not assume symmetry. Read Definition/Facts/Verification 1.1–4.1 against DJ relations, symmetrizer row convention, Chevalley maps, triangular decomposition, labels and dominance. The anti-map fixes q and K_h; moving toral factors through m=1-a_ij letters cancels the crossing exponent and gives (-1)^m q_i^-m q_j^-1 for both Serre images. Generator adjunctions extend by linearity and multiplication. A nonempty negative word is killed after applying sigma to the highest vector, giving uniqueness before transposition; distinct toral characters are orthogonal. Nondegeneracy on a weight space follows from global nondegeneracy and orthogonality, without identifying colliding labels. Existence and radical descent are explicitly deferred via justified_by to the level-2 Cartan-projection lemma, to be checked at its routed level. JKK (2.2)–(2.3), p.8, agrees with the linear convention. Normalization excludes a form on the zero module.

Accepted the exact skew commutator, balanced induction map and finite toral interpolation. Read Definition/Facts/Verification 1.1–4.1 with the previously reviewed skew, weight and DJ/triangular interfaces. Borel degree-zero projection is multiplicative because Q_+ is pointed; tensoring the triangular bimodule isomorphism gives U_q^- and a nonzero highest line, with finitely many words per root degree. Raising via the skew commutator kills the uE_i term only on the highest vector. The universal map is explicitly balanced and is label-preserving when its chosen vector has label lambda. All proper graded submodules have zero top component, so their sum stays proper and gives the unique graded-simple quotient. Arbitrary submodules are shown graded only for a separating pairing, using a finite product of commuting toral projections; no arbitrary-index AC enters. Later ordinary-simplicity/radical claims remain explicit downstream obligations.

Accepted the reader's corrected reference to the rank-one witness in Verification 2.2. Read the Definition and full Verification against negative-half grading, skew degree shift and tensor algebra. H and N give the augmentation row; conversely C and the recursion yield degree orthogonality by first-argument height induction, including vanishing target components. The same induction proves uniqueness, with finite word decompositions only. In one generator the recurrence leaves all B(1,F^m) free; c_1=1 gives B(1,F)=1 but B(F,1)=0, a valid nonsymmetry witness. Existence, symmetry, nondegeneracy and divided-power denominator normalization are explicitly delegated to the routed level-3 theorem via justified_by; JKK (6.5), p.23, matches the adjunction. No AC is used for this uniqueness construction.

Accepted the corrected inverse-K exponent, common-factor computation, explicit two-term induction and different-color swaps. Read Statement/Facts/Verification 1.1–4.1 with toral product, DJ, rank-one string and Pascal interfaces. For c=2t-a-b-2 and u=K_i q_i^(c+1), the three numerator products have the common W without assuming it invertible; equality follows from the two quantum addition identities. Induction on a shifts c by -2 in the no-contraction branch and uses T(t-b,1) in the contraction branch. t=0, t=a+1 and t=b endpoints are accounted for explicitly, and a=b=0 gives 1. Gaussian same-half coefficients lie in A. Triangular spanning terminates by lexicographic (total height, sign inversions), including i!=j swaps; it claims spanning only. Stanford lecture16 pp.9–10 supplies product/reordering background; the local calculation, rather than its faulty shift recurrence, is the evidence. No AC enters.

The item pre/post hashes agree; only contract evidence changed. Independently read Statement/Facts/Verification 1.1–5.1 and skew/integral/Pascal interfaces. The deletion coefficient on F_i^(r) is q_i^-(r-1), and the projector uses ordinary powers of e_i', essential for consecutive-term cancellation. Gauss inversion makes P_i kill every positive string F_i^(m)u with e_i'u=0. Successively removing the highest nonzero derivative gives a finite expansion; applying the largest derivative proves uniqueness and the explicit coefficient formula. On x=0 or e_i'x=0 the expansion is x_0=x. The integral half is preserved by deletion, the finite projector and both label shifts, using only Laurent-unit scalars and divided-power generators. Projection along F_i U_q^- follows after decomposition, without circularly assuming it. No global A-freeness or AC is used. JKK §6 p.23 identifies the projection/string decomposition, with its real-root ordinary-derivative convention.

Accepted the reader's declared Hopf-formula supplier and retained finite-cone, rather than finite-cardinality support. Read Statement/Facts/Verification 1.1–6.1, free-group/realization/minimal-realization interfaces and the exact DJ coproduct. A finite coordinate summand contains the upper labels and simple roots, hence all downward-cone labels. Evaluation makes j injective, auxiliary coroots primitive and their pairing perfect; mixed and Serre relations are unchanged because only the auxiliary torus is added. Relabeling and recovered toral characters give inverse graded-module recipes; no old-torus algebra embedding is claimed. Tensor formulas depend only on unchanged K_i,E_i,F_i and remain compatible. Finite rational linear algebra splits off a (2n-r)-dimensional minimal Cartan with root-killing central complement. Zero modules and an empty upper-label list cause no issue because all simple roots are still included. The chosen basis witnesses freeness; only finite choices of coordinates and complements are used.

Pre/post item hashes are identical; the reader enriched the contract. Read the Statement, Facts and Proof 1.1–3.1 against the integral generators and Chevalley involution supplier. Quantum factorials are bar-invariant; psi fixes both halves and tau exchanges them. On every toral-binomial factor both numerator and denominator acquire a minus sign, while tau reverses only commuting toral factors. Finite generated-algebra expressions therefore stay in U_A, with coefficients transformed inside A; involutivity proves equality rather than just inclusion. r=t=0 and negative c obey the same formulas. The semilinear tau here is distinct from the linear sigma used for normalized contravariant forms. No freeness, basis or choice assumption is used.

Accepted the reader's eta-annihilation explanation, symmetry dependency and negative-upper Gaussian argument. Read Statement/Facts/Verification 1.1–7.1 and all ten actual dependency interfaces. Verma coordinates give a well-defined homogeneous B; eta kills the left factors sigma(E_i) and K_h-q^lambda in sigma(J), while eta kills J itself, so replacing first or second arguments by their negative coordinates is legitimate. Generator contravariance and the previously proved uniqueness give symmetry without circularity. The graded radical is proper and every proper graded submodule pairs to zero by raising to its zero top component, proving radical=N and descent. Rank-one norms satisfy q_i^(m-2r+1)[m-r+1]/[r], including r=0 and r>m; the singular root component is one-dimensional. For ordinary simplicity a minimal label in a finite vector support is isolated by a homogeneous raising word, even when toral characters collide. Linear sigma preserves integral generators with its explicit q_i^(±r^2) scalars, and triangular spanning plus binom(-a,t)=(-1)^t binom(a+t-1,t) gives A-valued lattice pairings, without perfectness. This discharges the level-1 form definition's existence/radical obligation. No AC is used.

Accepted R-dependent Serre-rewrite coefficients, nilpotence in the quotient and corrected source attribution. Read Statement/Facts/Verification 1.1–4.1 against DJ/Verma/weight, integer and rank-one/reordering interfaces. The s_i are nonzero Verma string vectors killed by every E_j; triangular decomposition confines their generated submodules strictly below lambda, retaining the highest class and finite weight dimensions. The monic quantum Serre relation rewrites F_i^R F_j with left powers <1-a_ij and coefficients depending on R. Word induction transfers nilpotence of F_i on the highest class to all words, including a_ij=0 (N=1); the finite support bound makes E_i locally nilpotent. Minimal nonzero F-string length in any nonzero integrable highest module forces t_i=m_i+1, giving the universal quotient. m_i=0 and the empty word are covered; no false adjacent-root commutativity or AC is used. JKK Proposition 2.2 p.8 is cited as a statement, while the actual argument is local.

Accepted removal of the unspecified classical-adjoint analogy; the quantum separation proof is unchanged. Read Statement/Facts/Verification 1.1–4.1 and the exact generic-half theorem (i)–(ii), including its Q(z) rational-form clause and inherited AC. The producer supplies the two actual Serre presentations, matching negative-sign braided product and nondegenerate opposite-degree pairing. Degree-character rescaling by product(q_i-q_i^-1)^nu_i preserves both adjunctions and normalizes the generators. Primitive coproduct expansion has precisely the prefix-deletion scalars q^-(alpha_prefix,alpha_i), so the transported pairing obeys e_i' adjunction. Matching permutations prove symmetry; pairing against a word separates every nonzero homogeneous x and yields a height-many derivative sequence in the stated composition order. At nu=0 the empty sequence is the identity; one-step separation deliberately excludes degree zero. Bar transfers the result to e_i''. AC is inherited solely through the generic producer's formal embedding, explicitly declared in metadata and deps; no form theorem is circularly assumed. The oversized MIT scan was not read through the browser, and no classical-adjoint statement is retained.

Accepted the reader's field-valued Laurent coefficients, corrected stability/shift factors and Vandermonde-to-product multiplication. Read Statement/Facts/Verification 1.1–5.1 and all eight dependency interfaces. Evaluation K=z^n gives the symmetric Gaussian product; the weighted-subset Vandermonde recurrence and factorial cancellation yield exponent rs-jn after multiplication by B(n,r). Infinitely many distinct z^n establish the Laurent-polynomial identity. The shift follows by factoring common numerator factors, with K^-1 coefficient z^(-c+t-1). The two stability identities reduce positive/negative K powers, then shifts reduce c and t. Extremal exponents N+1 and -N prove the simple-torus A-basis; algebraic independence of the K_i gives the finite tensor-factor basis. Coset decomposition extends it to P^vee, with canonical minimum-coordinate representatives needing finite comparisons only, including nonsaturated L. r=s=t=0, negative c and the boundary N=0 are covered. No torsion-free-to-free inference over A, modified-algebra theorem or AC is used.

Accepted the corrected highest-generated R-lattice, noninversion of q-1, full integral-generator stability, finite-upper-label regularization, complex comparison and ordinary-simplicity dependency. Read Statement/Facts/Verification 1.1–6.1, all nineteen prerequisite interfaces and the complete local argument. R=Q[q]_(q-1) is a DVR/PID; finitely many words per label generate a torsion-free module, so the weight lattice is finite free with rank equal to generic dimension. Raising by commutators has integer quantum labels; every factorial is an R-unit and toral products have integer-upper regular scalars, giving stability under the entire U_A. Reduction yields classical Serre/Cartan relations without dividing by vanishing q_i-q_i^-1 and preserves integrability. On the auxiliary minimal Cartan, labels in one lambda-Q_+ stay distinct; a proper nonzero complex submodule has a maximal weight, hence a dominant primitive weight comparable to lambda in the same scalar Casimir eigenspace, contradicting the cited antichain lemma. This proves the rational fibre simple and identifies its character. Comparing finite label dimensions of the Serre quotient and its graded-simple quotient proves equality; Cartan-projection (iv) gives ordinary simplicity. Zero quotients are explicitly excluded and the highest lattice line survives reduction. The proof uses finite linear algebra, not a global integral basis or quantum semisimplicity. Berkeley finite-type comparison is background only; the general finite-GCM proof is local. Source-locator amendment: Berkeley Theorem 13.2.1.10 p.317 is finite-type background; removed the unsupported attribution of general local-q=1 deformation to the Stanford slides.

Accepted the reader's localization, exact toral factor, tensor-surjectivity and positive-quotient repairs; additionally corrected the Berkeley locator to §13.2.1 Theorem 13.2.1.10 p.317 and explicitly limited it to finite-type module background. Read Statement/Facts/Verification 1.1–4.1, all seventeen cited dependency interfaces, including generic-half rational PBW ranks and classical Serre/PBW. R inverts nonzero-at-1 coefficients, never q-1 or q_i-q_i^-1; [r]_i! and [s]_i are units. Finitely many ordinary words and generic/classical rank comparison identify each half fibre; inherited AC is explicit. H_i and K_i satisfy K_i^-1=K_i-(q_i-q_i^-1)H_i, and the exact binomial factor ([b]_i K_i+q_i^-b H_i)/[s]_i gives the toral presentation and basis. Field triangular injectivity and integral spanning give the R tensor isomorphism. The raw toral fibre is k[P^vee/2L] tensor k[H_i], while imposing every K_h=1 gives precisely k[H_i]. Central specialized K_h make the full augmentation ideal exactly the middle-factor ideal; classical PBW proves the full quotient is U(g_der), with rational descent to arbitrary characteristic-zero k. Standard rank-one K=-1 survives only in the unquotiented fibre. All local divisions are by units; t=0 and negative integer upper entries are valid.

Accepted the corrected multiplicative set generated by all quantum factorials. Read Statement/Facts/Verification 1.1–2.1 and every ten dependency interfaces, with the previously reviewed separation proof supplying the constructed homogeneous symmetric nondegenerate form, not merely its headline separation assertion. Peeling from the augmentation row proves uniqueness; component orthogonality plus finite support gives global nondegeneracy in both directions. Deletion on words has Laurent coefficients, proving A-valuedness on the word lattice. Rank-one divided norms satisfy b_m=q_i^-(m-1)b_(m-1)/[m]_i, so b_2=1/(1+q_i^2) is outside A (augmentation would require an integer reciprocal of 2). Any divided-power word has factorial-product denominators, giving the stated localization bound; S must contain finite products, as now stated. A constant right-adjunction against e_i'' fails at degree two after degree one forces c=1. The empty word and m=0,1 match normalization. AC is inherited only from the separation/generic-pairing supplier. This discharges the level-1 half-form definition's existence/symmetry/nondegeneracy obligation; no A-integrality on the larger divided lattice is asserted.

Accepted the corrected T(c,1)=K_i[c]_i+q_i^-c H_i identity, per-factor /s denominator, negative-upper Gaussian argument and explicit positive quotient. Read Statement/Facts/Verification 1.1–2.1 and all eight dependency interfaces. The toral quotient follows from the independently reviewed rational-local toral presentation, not from the AC-dependent half-rank argument. The lattice must be its own direct sum of intersections with label spaces; scalar Laurent polynomials then specialize on each summand and therefore on their tensor direct sum. Negative upper entries are (-1)^t binom(a+t-1,t), and t=0 gives 1. E/F and toral operators descend by U_A-stability, while the shifted T(±a_ij,1) identities give the Cartan commutators in the row convention. Neither lattice freeness nor a perfect pairing is required; zero or vanishing fibre pieces are allowed. K_h=1 is proved on type-one graded lattices and on the augmented toral quotient only, preserving the raw-fibre K=-1 boundary. No vanishing denominator is inverted or substituted.

Accepted the reader's correction from whole-cone support to support contained in lambda-Q_+. Read Statement/Facts/Verification 1.1–2.1 with all nine prerequisite interfaces, especially the fully reviewed Serre quotient, local deformation and Cartan form proofs. The dominant singular relations give a nonzero integrable quotient; the graded-simple quotient factors because its maximal graded submodule contains every proper singular-vector submodule. Equal classical characters on finite label pieces make the quotient map injective; homogeneous nondegenerate form and finite-support raising give ordinary simplicity. Any nonzero integrable cyclic highest module receives the unique highest-vector map and kills the minimal rank-one singular powers; ordinary simplicity makes that surjection an isomorphism. At lambda=0 in standard sl2, the quotient is one-dimensional with support {0}, disproving equality with the infinite cone and confirming the reader correction. No global A-freeness, crystal basis or quantum semisimplicity is assumed. The changed support interface requires focused direct-consumer checks and routing of outside-batch defects, recorded separately below.

Accepted the reader's Berkeley source correction, and amended the title to include finite-dimensional weight spaces, matching Statement (a); refuter:5:1 is confirmed fatal as an unsupported broader advertised scope. Read Statement/Facts/Proof 1.1–6.1 and all fourteen dependency interfaces. Finite rank-one cyclic hulls are stable; the explicit central rank-one Casimir separates highest integer strings and proves their finite complete reducibility locally. Finite upper cones and finite label dimensions make positive cyclic spans finite; the top bound and rank-one symmetry bound both ends of each fixed simple-root line, making the restricted sigma-dual integrable. A maximal label in a finite graded Borel-stable generating space supplies a simple highest submodule; evaluation against its normalized highest dual vector and the homogeneous nondegenerate form yield a grading-preserving retraction. Dimension induction splits the finite generated case; finite simple-sum submodule induction also covers ordinary ungraded submodules. The arbitrary module is a sum of these finite sums, and AC selects a maximal independent family only in the final step. Zero modules give the empty sum; incomparable maximal labels do not affect the retraction. All finite-cone and finite-weight hypotheses of the actual proof are retained. Berkeley Theorem 13.2.1.10 and Corollary 13.2.1.11 pp.317–318 were read through their proofs and support finite-type background, not the full local statement.

decisions.evidence: The post-reader title omitted Statement (a), finite-dimensional weight spaces. Added that exact hypothesis; the mathematical Statement and Proof are unchanged and independently reviewed.
The summary of complete reducibility omitted the cited proposition's finite-dimensional label-weight-space hypothesis. Added that hypothesis; all other page claims agree with the current local items.

Accepted the reader's integral-form source qualification and removal of unused flatness. Additionally repaired F2's dimension-only explanation: total root components can be infinite-dimensional, so injectivity follows from the cited supplier's factorwise half/torus isomorphisms and intertwined PBW tensor decompositions, not an equality of cardinal dimensions. Corrected Berkeley background to Theorem 13.2.1.10 p.317 rather than attributing the local DVR argument to it. Read Statement/Facts/Verification 1.1–2.1 with all ten dependency interfaces and the full rational-local and graded-lattice suppliers. A->k at q=1 factors through R; halves specialize componentwise, and the central K_h augmentation ideal yields the exact positive full quotient. On an arbitrary stable label-graded lattice, diagonal Laurent scalars specialize without freeness, and the integral Serre identities reduce coefficientwise. K=-1 remains a valid unquotiented rank-one character, showing why augmentation is required; extra Cartan directions are module label actions rather than fabricated integral generators. AC enters only through generic half rank comparison. No Statement or Definition changed.

Accepted the reader's corrected EF^(2) coefficient T(-1,1) and identification of the nontrivial a=b=2 toral factors. Read Example/Facts/Verification 1.1–2.1 and all five cited supplier interfaces. Factorial arithmetic gives E^(2)E=[3]E^(3) and F^(2)F^(2)=binom(4,2)F^(4); direct Gaussian expansion gives q^-4+q^-2+2+q^2+q^4. The b=2 numerator sum factors by [2], which cancels against q^2-q^-2 and yields precisely T(-1,1), rather than an undivided sum of shifted binomials. The general reordering gives t=0,1,2 factors 1,T(-2,1),T(0,2). Scalar values at integer weights reduce to m,m-2,binom(m,2), through Laurent products and the explicit quotient/lattice supplier. Empty divided powers and negative integer weight values respect those conventions. This is finite rank-one algebra with no AC; Stanford pp.9–10 matches the product and equal-exponent reordering background.

Accepted the reader's explicit standard rank-one datum, distinction between ordinary and divided bases, largest-index raising argument and integral/nondominant wording. Read Example/Facts/Verification 1.1–3.1 and all six cited interfaces. The ordinary basis has E coefficient [t][m-t+1], whereas divided basis has [m-t+1]; K weights are m-2t in both. For m>=0 the singular tail beginning at m+1 is stable and exactly generated by F^(m+1)v; the quotient has m+1 basis vectors. Raising a finite sum from its largest occupied index produces a nonzero top vector, proving ordinary simplicity. For every m<0 the same coefficients never vanish, including m=-1 where they are -[t]; F remains nonnilpotent, proving infinite dimension and nonintegrability. m=0 is trivial, and T=0 uses the empty raising product. Dominance, not integrality, is the essential failed hypothesis. No AC enters this finite-word argument.

Accepted the reader's full divided-power and toral matrix stability proof. Additionally replaced 'base change is exact on the free lattice' by base change of its explicit free basis: k at q=1 is not flat over A, and no exactness assertion is needed. Read Example/Facts/Verification 1.1–2.1 with all seven dependency interfaces. The vectors v_t are field-independent, giving the A-basis directly; F^(r) and E^(r) have coefficients binom(t+r,r) and binom(m-t+r,r), and vanish at their respective endpoints. K has Laurent-unit diagonal entries and all T(c,s) have integral Gaussian values, including negative upper labels, proving stability under the entire U_A and equality V_A=U_Av_0. Tensoring the displayed direct sum gives k^(m+1) with the stated classical coefficients and Cartan labels. The matrices satisfy the classical commutators and largest-index raising proves simplicity; m=0 gives the one-dimensional trivial case and the m=2 displayed triple is exact. This specific rank-one freeness uses the explicit basis, not a torsion-free argument over A or the general integral PBW theorem. No Statement or Definition changed; no AC is used.

Accepted the reader's correction that the numerator and denominator vanish while T(0,1) itself has a nonzero specialized operator, and the explicit binom(2,1) witness replacing a blanket Gaussian claim. Read Statement refuted/Facts/Counterexample 1.1–2.1 and all seven dependency interfaces. In L(1), K=diag(q,q^-1) reduces to identity but T(0,1)=diag(1,-1), so separate numerator/denominator substitution gives undefined 0/0 and loses the coroot action. The scalar [2]=q+q^-1 specializes to 2, and the b>=1 string coefficient equals the integral toral binomial T(1-b,1) with value m-b+1. These equalities are established at generic q and specialized as integral elements, with no inverse of a zero specialized denominator. The explicit divided lattice from the prior example supplies the admissible stable lattice. The zero-label scalar can vanish, but m=±1 provides the required nonzero witness; characteristic zero preserves 1!=-1. No AC is used. Berkeley Theorem 13.2.1.10 p.317 shows the same coroot operator evaluation by factoring, consistent with this local counterexample.
